0. FOREWORD
Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 30 September 1975, after the draft finalized by the Spices and Condiments Sectional Committee had been approved by the Agricultural and Food Products Division Council. 0.2 It is hoped that followed by different national disputes. this standard laboratories, would thereby unify the methods avoiding national of test as and inter-

0.1This

0.3 This standard is based on the methods of test as compiled at the Central Food Laboratory, Calcutta; Public Health Laboratory, Poona; and Central Food Technological Research Institute, Mysore. Subsequently, they were recommended by the Central Committee for Food Standards, Ministry of Health also. In compiling this standard assistance has also been derived from the following publications: INDIA. MINISTRY OF HEALTH. British Pharmacopoeia of India-1955

UNITED KINGDOM.

Pharmacopoeia Pharmacopoeia

of 1963 of USA1936

UNITED STATES OF AMERICA.

0.4 This standard is essentially meant for pure asafoetida. However, keeping in view the caution given (see Note ), the methods may also be applied to compounded asafoetida with certain amount of caution. NOTE- Some workers have reported that presence of wheat flour/rice flour/turmeric interfere with the tests given in 7.1.1 and 7.1.2. Work on other flours is in progress. While reporting the result of a test or analysis made in accordance this standard, if the final value, observed or calculated, is to be rounded off, it shall be done in accordance with IS : 2-1960*.

3.2.1 Preparation of Samfile - Mix carefully the using the grinding mill, grind a small quantity of it. Then, grind quickly an amount slightly larger Avoid undue heating of the apparatus the test. carefully so as to avoid stratification. Transfer the previously dried sample container and immediately 3.2.2 prepared

Test Portion-Weigh to the nearest 0.001 sample into the tared flat-bottomed dish.

3.2.3 Determination - Pour about 2 ml of ethanol on the material in the tared dish ( 3.1.1 ) and ignite it. When the ethanol is burnt off, heat the dish carefully over a small flame to char the material. Then ignite in the muffle furnace ( 3.1.2 ) at 550 & 25�C for 2 hours. Cool and wet the ash with several drops of water, evaporate carefully to dryness and heat in the muffle furnace for further 1 hour at 550 f 25'C. If the wetting shows the ash to be carbon-free, remove the dish to a desiccator containing fresh, efficient desiccant, allow to cool to room temperature and weigh without delay. If the wetting shows the presence of carbon, repeat the wetting and heating until no specks of carbon are visible and ignite in the muffle furnace for 1 hour after the disappearance of carbon. If carbon is still visible, leach the ash with hot water, filter through the ashless filter wash the filter paper thoroughly, transfer the filter paper paper, and contents to the ashing dish, dry and ignite in the muffle furnace at

Repeat these operations until the difference in mass between two successive weighings is less than 0.002 g. Record the lowest mass. Retain the total ash for determining the water-soluble ash and the acid-insoluble ash. 3.3 Calculation Total ash ( on dry basis ), = (&--MM,) percent by mass where M2 = mass in g of the dish and total ash, MO = mass in g of the.empty dish, M1 = mass in g of the dish and test portion, and H = moisture content of the sample as received ( see 4.1 ). 4. 4.1 Determine the amount of moisture in the sample by the toluene distillation method ( see 10 of IS : 1797-1973* ). 5. ACID-INSOLUBLE ASH

5.1 Procedure L Boil the ash ( see 3.2.3) with 25 ml of dilute hydrochloric acid ( 1 part concentrated hydrochloric acid + 2.5 parts water ) for 5 minutes covering the basin with a watch-glass. Filter the insoluble matter on an ashless filter paper or tared Gooch crucible. Wash with hot distilled water until washings are acid-free. Ignite, cool and weigh. Calculate the percentage of acid-insoluble ash from the mass of the sample taken ( 3.2.3 ). 6. ALCOHOLIC EXTRACT

6.1 Procedure - Place accurately weighed about 2 g of asafoetida ( 10 g of compounded asafoetida ) in a tared extraction thimble and extract with alcohol ( 90 percent by volume ) in either a Soxhlet or other suitable extraction apparatus for about 3 hours. Dry the insoluble residue at 100�C for 30 minutes or until constant mass is obtained.

7.1 Colophony - The consignment should be rejected, when the sample fails in all the three tests as given in 7.1.1, 7.1.2 and 7.1.3 (see also 0.4 ).
7.1.1 Acetic Anhydride Method-Dissolve about O-1 g of asafoetida ( or O-5 g of compounded asafoetida ) in 10 ml of acetic anhydride. Heat gently, cool, and add one drop of sulphuric acid. A bright purplish-red colour, rapidly changing to violet, shall be produced, if colophony is present. 7.1.2 Copfier Acetate Method - Triturate about 1 g of asafoetida ( or 5 g of compounded asafoetida ) with 10 ml of light petroleum ( bp 40 to 50�C ) Filter and add to the filtrate 10 ml of a fresh O-5 percent for 2 minutes. ( m/u ) aqueous solution of copper acetate. Shake well and allow the liquids to separate. The petroleum layer shall show green colour if colophony is present. 7.1.3 Thin Layer Chromatography ( TLC) Method

7.1.3.1 Principal - The test is based on isolation and identification of abietic acid, a major constituent of colophony resin by TLC. Abietic acid spots are visualized by spraying with Halphen-Hicks reagent. 7.1.3.2 Reagents BP 40 to 60�C. ( 9 : 1 ). reagent ) carbon tetrachloride and benezene-methanol a) Petroleum ether b) Solvent -

c) Spray reagent ( Ha&hen- Hicks phenol (2: 1).

d) Abietic acid solution, standard - Dissolve good quality colophony resin in 98 percent acetic acid and reflux the solution for 2 hours. Filter, cool and allow the crystals to separate out. Recrystallize in 95 percent ethanol. Dissolve 0.1 g of recrystallized abietic acid in 100 ml of One microlitre of this solution is petroleum ether ( 40 to 60�C ). equivalent to 1 pg of abietic acid.
NOTE- Instead of standard abietic acid, if not available, 10 ~1 of 1 percent solution of colophony resin may be used.

7.1.3.3

Apparatus 20 X 10 cm.

a) Glass plates b) TLC chamber 7.1.3.4
Procedure

a) Extraction - Take about 0.1 g of asafoetida or 0.5 g of compounded asafoetida and triturate or mix intimately with 10 ml of petroleum Keep the filtrate in a stoppered test tube. ether for 5 minutes. b) Preparation of thin-Layer plates - Coat the glass plates with a slurry of silica gel in water ( 1 : 2 ) to a thickness of 250 pm. Allow the plates to set at room temperature for 30 minutes. Activate the Store the plates in a plates at 100�C for one hour in an air-oven. desiccator before use. c) Spotting and development - Spot the following on silica gel plate leaving 1 cm from the starting point: 1) 10 ~1 of sample extract [7.1.3.4(a) 1. 2) 10 ~1 of standard abietic acid [7.1.3.2(d) 1.

3) 10 ~1 of sample extract + microlitre of standard abietic acid. Develop the plate in ascending manner in a TLC: chamber with the mobile solvent [ 7.1.3.2(b) 1. When the solvent front ascends 10 cm from the starting point, remove the plate and dry in air for 30 minutes. d) Detection of spots - Spray the plate with the Halphen-Hicks reagent [ see 7.1.3.2(c) 1. Expose the plate to bromine vapour in a saturated bromine chamber. Within three minutes blue/purple spots of abietic acid develop ( Rf = 0.75 approx ). Remove the plate quickly and examine the spots in visible light. Blue/purple spot in the sample shall show that it contains abietic acid and, therefore, colophony resin. e) Sensitivity 5 pg of abietic acid can be detected by this method.

7.2 Galbanum - Add dilute hydrochloric acid dropwise to 10 ml of the alcoholic extract ( see 6.1) of the sample until faint turbidity appears. Appearance of a bluish-green colour in the mixture which fades on standing shall indicate absence of galbanum. 7

Ii?4 t 7807 - 1975 7.3 Ammoniacum 7.3.1 Reagent
7.3.1.1 Sodium hvpobromite reagent -freshly of sodium hydroxide-in 75 ml of water, adding up to 100 ml with water. prepared by dissolving 20 g 5 ml of bromine and making

7.3.2 Procedure - Mix well about 4 g of the asafoetida ( 20 g of compounded asafoetida ) with 90 ml of distilled water in a mortar. Filter and Mix 2 ml of the extract with 5 ml of water make up the filtrate to 100 ml. in a test tube and add 5 ml of the hypobromite reagent cautiously down the side of the test tube so as to form a separate layer. Non-appearance of red colour in the mixture shall show absence of ammoniacum. 7.4 Other Foreign Resins - Add a few drops of 9 percent aqueous ferric chloride solution to 5 ml of the alcoholic extract ( see 6.1 ). Appearance of olive-green colour in the mixture shall indicate absence of Appearance of blackish precipitate or most foreign resins in asafoetida. colouration in the mixture shall show absence of foreign resins in compounded asafoetida. 8. STARCH examination reveals the presence of added starch, using diastase as acid inversion gives erroneous

8.1 If the microscopic it should be estimated results.

8.2 Procedure-Thoroughly extract about 5 g of asafoetida ( 25 g of compounded asafoetida ) with light petroleum, then with alcohol and dry. Wash the residue into a loo-ml volumetric flask with ammonia-free water and heat on the water-bath for 30 minutes. Add 8.2.1 Enzymatic Method - Cool the residue obtained above to 55%. 0.1 g of diastase dissolved in a little water and maintain at about 55�C for 3 hours. Cool, add 5 ml of the sodium hydroxide solution, dilute to 100 ml and estimate the sugar produced using Fehling's solution (see 6.1.8 of IS : 4706-1968* ). Calculate as starch ( dextrose x 0.90 = starch ), assuming that wheat flour (the most common in compounded asafoetida ) contains 72 percent of starch.
